blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Global Britain, at its best, is a multicultural workplace that draws on colleagues from every corner of the world and treats that mix as a strategic asset rather than a challenge to be managed. The senior leaders who do this well are not performing diversity — they are running businesses in which different perspectives, languages and life experiences sharpen every important decision.

Getting it right is less about programmes and more about attention. Who speaks first in the room? Whose idea gets remembered, and whose gets quietly attributed to someone else? Whose holidays is the company sensitive to, and whose are simply forgotten? These tiny signals, aggregated over months, tell the team who belongs and who is merely tolerated.

The best executives pay attention to the small signals. They correct, quietly and consistently, the small exclusions. They make sure every voice has genuine space and every contribution genuine credit. Done well over years, this quiet attention produces teams that feel like no other place those colleagues have worked — and a competitive advantage that is very hard for a more monocultural competitor to copy.

items.q: How do the leaders described in the text treat a multicultural workforce?
options: As a marketing opportunity for the brand
As a temporary experiment to be reviewed
As a compliance requirement imposed from outside
As a strategic asset rather than a challenge to be managed
items.why: "treats that mix as a strategic asset rather than a challenge to be managed."

items.q: According to the text, getting diversity right depends mostly on…
options: hiring quotas set by the board
items.why: "Getting it right is less about programmes and more about attention."

items.q: What do the "tiny signals, aggregated over months" reveal to the team?
options: Which departments are the most profitable
Who belongs and who is merely tolerated
items.why: "These tiny signals… tell the team who belongs and who is merely tolerated."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Whose idea gets remembered is a meaningful signal.
Inclusion is built through small, consistent corrections.
Multicultural teams can be a durable competitive advantage.
A visible diversity programme, on its own, guarantees real inclusion.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que inclusão vem da atenção diária, não de programas — 'performing diversity' é o oposto do que ele defende.

items.q: That the advantage is "very hard for a more monocultural competitor to copy" suggests that…
options: monocultural firms are always more profitable
the advantage comes from years of practice, not from a policy that can be bought
diversity has no measurable business value
items.why: Inferência: 'done well over years' e 'hard to copy' apontam para uma capacidade construída no tempo, não replicável de imediato.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando o CEO sobre inclusão. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Can I be direct? The photographs are excellent. Your leadership pages look like the United Nations, and I know that took real effort. But representation in a photograph and influence in a room are two very different things, and I think you already suspect that.

Here is what I would watch for over the next quarter. In your executive meetings, notice whose idea gets built on and whose gets politely nodded at and then forgotten. Notice who you interrupt without thinking. When a proposal from one of your quieter regional colleagues gets repeated back by someone more senior, notice who ends up receiving the credit for it. None of that shows up in a diversity report, and all of it decides whether people stay.

My advice is unglamorous. Do not launch another programme this year. Instead, do three small things consistently: make sure every voice has genuine space, make sure every contribution keeps its author's name attached, and be sensitive to holidays and customs you might otherwise forget.

Do that quietly for eighteen months and you will have something a monocultural competitor simply cannot copy. Do the photographs and skip the attention, and you will have turnover you can't explain.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What distinction does Sophie draw at the start of the talk?
options: Between representation in a photograph and influence in a room
items.why: "representation in a photograph and influence in a room are two very different things."

items.q: What does Sophie advise the CEO NOT to do this year?
items.why: "Do not launch another programme this year."

items.q: Which of the three small things does Sophie recommend?
options: Interrupt less-senior colleagues to save time
Make sure every contribution keeps its author's name attached
items.why: "make sure every contribution keeps its author's name attached" é uma das três coisas.

items.q: When Sophie says an idea "gets politely nodded at and then forgotten," she is pointing to…
options: a subtle form of exclusion that no report captures
items.why: Inferência: é exatamente o 'small exclusion' — a pessoa está presente mas sua voz não tem peso real.

items.q: What does Sophie imply will happen if the CEO does "the photographs and skips the attention"?
options: The board will cut the budget
People will leave for reasons the CEO can't explain
items.why: Inferência: 'turnover you can't explain' — sem inclusão real, a rotatividade sobe sem causa aparente nos relatórios.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board finally treats its multilingual desk as a strategic asset." A strategic asset is…
options: a cost that must be justified each year
a temporary project with a fixed end date
a resource that creates lasting competitive value
a legal obligation imposed by regulators
items.why: Strategic asset = ativo estratégico: algo que gera valor competitivo duradouro.

items.q: "A leader who is merely performing diversity is…"
options: staging it for appearances without real inclusion
delegating it to the HR team
items.why: To perform diversity = encenar diversidade: aparência sem substância.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Diverse perspectives ___ every important decision instead of blurring it."
items.why: To sharpen = afiar: as perspectivas tornam a decisão mais precisa, não a atrasam.

items.q: "Small slights, aggregated over months, drive people out." Aggregated here means…
items.why: To aggregate = somar/acumular: os pequenos sinais se acumulam ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "That edge is very hard for a ___ competitor to copy."
items.why: Monocultural = de uma só cultura, o oposto do time diverso que gera a vantagem.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre inclusão e liderança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CEO agreed to sign off on the new inclusion policy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the mentoring scheme office by office." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the quota idea." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They promised change but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A better photograph won't move the needle on inclusion." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
